claim_summaries: Finite-net approximate fixed states of a tracial corrected broadcaster admit an explicit finite-outcome EB compressor using the primary finite-tuple almost-commuting theorem; the residual rate depends badly on net size N.
Any finite-outcome EB reconstruction on a theta-sandwich family can be coarsened to at most (ceil(2 theta/delta)+1)^N outcomes at added trace error 2a+delta/2.
For supplied bistochastic instruments, an exact factor-two SOS yields the sharper EB residual bound and the same finite alphabet compression.
The sourced copy-ladder family rules out an unconditional dimension-blind broadcast-error-to-EB-error modulus; it requires growing covering complexity and is not a fixed-sandwich counterexample.
